original_question: If G is a planar subcubic graph, must its HL-index R(G) always be at most 1?
target_in_paper: Mohar’s HL-index conjecture for planar subcubic graphs: stated in detailed form as Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1 of A note on median eigenvalues of subcubic graphs, and restated in the survey Unsolved Problems in Spectral Graph Theory as Conjecture 22 in Section 19.2.
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the right open problem: the quantifier is over planar subcubic graphs, the invariant is the HL-index R(G), and the claimed bound is exactly 1. That is the substance of Mohar’s conjecture.
missing_details: The draft does not define the HL-index R(G). In the paper, it is defined from the adjacency eigenvalues of G.
The graph should be specified to be a simple graph, since that is the standing setup in the paper.
One should state that if G has order n and adjacency eigenvalues lambda_1(G) >= ... >= lambda_n(G), counted with multiplicity, then the relevant indices are h = floor((n+1)/2) and l = ceil((n+1)/2).
The exact definition R(G) = max{|lambda_h(G)|, |lambda_l(G)|} should be included to make the question stand-alone.
The draft leaves implicit that the eigenvalues are those of the adjacency matrix, not of the Laplacian or another graph matrix.
Subcubic should be made explicit as the degree condition Delta(G) <= 3.
The paper’s conjecture does not add a connectedness assumption here, so the stand-alone version should quantify over every simple planar graph with maximum degree at most 3.
refined_question: Let G be a simple planar graph of order n with maximum degree Delta(G) <= 3, and let lambda_1(G) >= ... >= lambda_n(G) be the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix, counted with multiplicity. If h = floor((n+1)/2) and l = ceil((n+1)/2), define the HL-index of G by R(G) = max{|lambda_h(G)|, |lambda_l(G)|}. Is it true that R(G) <= 1 for every such graph G?
justification: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s intended question, but it is not fully self-contained because it leaves R(G) undefined. In the technical paper devoted to this topic, the introduction defines the adjacency-eigenvalue notation and then states exactly this open problem as Conjecture 1.1. The nearby Theorem 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 give two verified families—subcubic graphs containing K_{2,3} as a subgraph, and K_4-minor-free subcubic graphs—so they help fix the local scope, but they are partial results rather than reformulations of the conjecture. The survey paper you listed repeats the same conjecture later as Conjecture 22, but the sharper stand-alone wording comes from the detailed introductory setup of the technical paper.
